title: Independently check #4610's warp substitution: 34 of 72 G maps changed, all invertible and frame-transporting; 17,453 scalar opcodes unchanged, 422 labels; 3,298 paid calls (no new κ)
body:
Independent Python check of intqwq's #4610 warp-substitution claims. The comparison runs between its vendored emitted word (blob `79dad65b`, SHA256-pinned) and PR4470's word from main's pinned constructor. **Every checked claim holds.** No new κ.

`research/pr4610-warp-substitution-check/verify.py` uses the standard library only and takes about 2 s.

## Results

- **Warp maps.** All 72 G maps are invertible on F₂⁹ and map their input frame **onto** their output frame. Exactly **34** changed, and op, lender and B_pos are unchanged for all 72.
- **Scalars.** In both orientations, all **17,453 scalar opcodes and coefficients are unchanged, in order**, and exactly **422** frame labels differ.
- **Paid calls.** Climbs go from 3,302 to 3,290, so paid calls go from **3,310 to 3,298**.
- **Other events.** Adapter, warp, phase and centre counts are unchanged.

Together with #4614 (endpoint frames and profile) and #4615 (raw crossing), every structural and arithmetic statement of #4610 checked so far holds.

## Not covered

- absolute phases and monomial lowering;
- the symbolic endpoint identity;
- contract admissibility of generator substitution, which is the maintainers' call.

Credit: intqwq (#4610) and Cinna Davis (#4470). Ryanson Jonathan, with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) assistance.
